title: Witnessed adjunctions and the exceptional comparison on one affine chart
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. For every finite-type $k$-scheme $S$, let $\nu_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}\to S_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and let $\mathcal C(S)=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(S,A)$ be the witnessed category [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]: an object consists of $K\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $K_e\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_S^*K_e\cong K$, and morphisms are the morphisms of the underlying pro-etale complexes. For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $v:S\to R$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], use compact support $Rv_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. At a chosen compactification write $v_e^\times$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint and write $G_v=\nu_S^*v_e^\times R\nu_{R,*}$ for the transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], initially on bounded-below objects. Then $Rv_!$ and $G_v$ admit lifts to $\mathcal C(S)\to\mathcal C(R)$ and $\mathcal C(R)\to\mathcal C(S)$, respectively, with natural adjunction bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(R)}(Rv_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(S)}(M,G_vN).$$
Their underlying functors and bijections are independent of compactification under the canonical comparison isomorphisms. If $M\cong\nu_S^*M_e$ and $N\cong\nu_R^*N_e$ are the specified witnesses, their images have witnesses $Rv_{!,e}M_e$ and $v_e^\times N_e$, both bounded below.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes. Choose an affine open immersion $g:V\hookrightarrow Y$, put $X_V=X\times_YV$, and write $h:X_V\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$ for the projections. Choose an affine open immersion $u':U\hookrightarrow X_V$, an integer $d\geq0$, and a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^d_V$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with projection $\pi:T\to V$ such that $f_Vu'=\pi i$; put $u=hu'$. Open inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves $\mathcal C$ and the witness restricts to the ordinary etale restriction. There is a natural isomorphism on $\mathcal C(V)$
$$L(u')^*G_{f_V}N\cong G_iG_\pi N.$$
For every bounded constructible $L\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical base-open and chart comparisons give
$$Lh^*G_fL\cong G_{f_V}Lg^*L,\qquad Lu^*G_fL\cong G_iG_\pi Lg^*L.$$
All these comparisons are comparisons in the witnessed categories; no preservation of bounded constructibility by $G_f$, $G_i$ or $G_\pi$ is assumed in these assertions.

proof.text: All schemes occurring in the assertion are Noetherian: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to open subschemes. Here a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. In particular all targets are quasi-compact; intersections of affine opens are open Noetherian subschemes and hence quasi-compact, so the schemes are quasi-separated. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies the chosen compactifications for separated finite-type maps. For the chart, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] applies to $f_V$ and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] to $h$. The open maps are quasi-compact since their sources and all affine-open inverse images are Noetherian opens. They are separated and of finite type, and the same holds for the closed map $i$, the affine-space projection $\pi$, and their displayed composites. Consequently the Noetherian and compactifiability hypotheses of the etale results used below hold, without requiring $X$ or $Y$ to be separated over $k$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: geometric hypotheses for compact support and the chart

proof.text: Write $F_v=Rv_{!,e}$ and $H_v=v_e^\times$ on the ordinary etale categories. The adjunction $F_v\dashv H_v$ is [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Its restriction has both functors taking values in $D^+$: compact support is the bounded-below functor in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], and [lem-etale-upper-shriek-quasicompact-bounded-below] applies to $H_v$ because the target $R$ is quasi-compact by step 1. The latter assertion is only bounded-below preservation, with a possible lower-bound shift; it asserts no constructibility preservation. Apply this also to $f_V,i,\pi$ and the open chart maps. In particular $i_e^\times\pi_e^\times N_e$ is bounded below whenever $N_e$ is.

u_{R,*} eta$. Apply $C_SH_v$ to obtain $C_SH_vN_e\cong G_vN$. Step 2 supplies bounded-below witnesses $F_vM_e$ and $H_vN_e$; [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] ensures their comparison pullbacks are bounded below as well. These constructions define object lifts. On arrows use exactly $Rv_!$ and $G_v$ on the underlying pro-etale arrow; the definition of morphisms in [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory] imposes no extra witness map. Identity and composition laws therefore remain the underlying functor laws.

source.place: Step 1: retain actual etale witnesses for both functors

proof.text:
Using the witnesses from step 3, full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and the ordinary adjunction [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], the required bijection is the chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(R)}(Rv_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(R_e)}(F_vM_e,N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(S_e)}(M_e,H_vN_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C(S)}(M,G_vN).$$
All four Hom sets are well typed by steps 2 and 3. Every arrow between witnessed objects corresponds to a unique etale arrow by full faithfulness, so the naturality of the comparisons and the etale adjunction proves naturality for every underlying arrow, not just arrows initially presented with etale lifts. Thus this is an actual adjunction of the two lifted functors.

source.place: Step 1: adjunction on the witnessed categories

proof.text: On the stated domain, [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] gives the canonical compact-support comparisons and their cocycle. The ordinary etale versions are those of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. At two compactifications, their $D^+$ right adjoints from step 2 are compared by the counit-compatible uniqueness isomorphism of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], after identifying the left adjoints. Applying $C_S$ and the witness-unit identifications of step 3 gives comparisons of $G_v$. The Hom chain in step 4 commutes with these maps: the middle bijection does so by counit compatibility, and the outer bijections are natural comparison isomorphisms. Identity and composition of right comparisons follow because both composites are counit-compatible and uniqueness makes them equal. This proves the asserted independence, including the underlying bijections.

source.place: Step 1: independence of compactification under the canonical comparisons

proof.text: For any of the open immersions $j:W\hookrightarrow T$, constant-coefficient pullback is exact on both sites by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Thus $Lj^*=j^*$ acts termwise and preserves a lower bound. Apply the natural inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] termwise to the witness $C_TM_e\cong M$: it gives $C_W(j_e^*M_e)\cong j^*M$. This constructs the claimed restricted witness and the functor on $\mathcal C$. The identity and composition compatibilities in that comparison identify restriction along $u=hu'$ with successive restriction along $h$ and $u'$.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: open inverse image in the witnessed categories

proof.text:
For $N_e\in D^+(V_e,A)$ set $B=i_e^\times\pi_e^\times N_e$ and $Q=(u'_e)^*(f_V)_e^\times N_e$. By steps 2 and 6 both are in $D^+(U_e,A)$. Apply [lem-sf-etale-chart-adjoint-comparison] with $f=f_V$, $s=u'$, $v=\mathrm{id}_V$, $p=\pi$ and $K=N_e$; step 1 checks every geometric hypothesis and $f_Vu'=\pi i$ is the chosen equality. It supplies the natural bijection $\Theta_H:\operatorname{Hom}(H,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)$, the inverse of the bijection displayed in that node. Explicitly its forward chain is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(u'_!H,(f_V)_e^\times N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(f_V)_{!,e}u'_!H,N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R\pi_{!,e}i_*H,N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B).$$
Here the cited node supplies the normalized compact-support compositor as well as the adjunctions: we use its stated natural Hom bijection, not an unstated identification of unbounded representing objects.

source.place: Step 1: the chart comparison from compact-support composition and open adjunction

proof.text: Evaluate step 7 at the two representing objects, which is allowed because both are bounded below. Set $a=\Theta_Q(1_Q):Q\to B$ and $b=\Theta_B^{-1}(1_B):B\to Q$. Naturality in $H$ gives $\Theta_H(t)=a\circ t$ and $\Theta_H^{-1}(z)=b\circ z$. Hence $a\circ b=1_B$ and $b\circ a=1_Q$ by the inverse identities of the bijections. The naturality in $N_e$ gives $B(\phi)\circ a_{N_e}=a_{N'_e}\circ Q(\phi)$ for every $\phi:N_e\to N'_e$, so $a$ is a natural isomorphism. Its definition as successive transposes of the normalized compact-support comparison also fixes its canonical adjunction normalization.

source.place: Step 1: transport the chart comparison without a constructible preservation assertion

proof.text: For the final assertion, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] puts the bounded constructible $L$ in $\mathcal C(Y)$. Step 6 puts $Lg^*L$ in $\mathcal C(V)$ without requiring a constructible output from any exceptional functor. Apply only the independent bounded-class clause of [cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general], with $g:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $h:X_V\hookrightarrow X$. It states that the canonical map $Lh^*G_fL\to G_{f_V}Lg^*L$ is invertible for this bounded constructible input, with no unrestricted ambient datum. Steps 3 and 6 show that its source and target carry etale-origin witnesses; their Hom sets are the underlying pro-etale Hom sets, so its inverse is also a morphism of the witnessed categories. Restrict it along $u'$ and compose with step 9 at $N=Lg^*L$. Using $u=hu'$ and the composition compatibility of step 6 gives $Lu^*G_fL\cong G_iG_\pi Lg^*L$, as required.
